sector_model: nonfinancial data, analytics and credit ratings (not a bank or insurer); GAAP earnings with divestiture gains flagged, FCF after capex, debt from senior notes, buyback-reduced equity
thesis: Moody's (ratings via MIS, data and analytics via MA) reported Q3 2026 revenue +1% to 2,023M (organic constant currency +3%), adjusted operating margin 52.6%, adjusted diluted EPS 4.14 (+6%), MA ARR 3,688M (+8%). Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance: high-single-digit revenue growth, adjusted EPS 16.50 to 17.00, FCF 2.7 to 2.9B, buybacks up to 3.0B. Close 505.67 on 2026-11-06 (NYSE) gives market cap about 87.2B; guided GAAP EPS midpoint 16.25 gives about 31x, adjusted midpoint 16.75 about 30x, TTM FCF 2,977M (3.4%). Strong franchise with 99% recurring MA revenue and high margins; price already reflects it.
counterthesis: Revenue growth was only 1% in Q3 (organic 3%); MIS transaction revenue fell 5% with high yield down 40% and leveraged loans down 27%, and the stock is near its post-earnings high (505.67 vs 477.27 on 10-28, +5.9%). GAAP earnings are flattered by divestiture gains (296M pre-tax in 9M26, about 1.18 per share guided for the year): TTM GAAP net income 2,883M includes them. Moody's shareholders' equity is only 3.27B after 2.55B of 9M repurchases, which outpaces guided free cash flow and was partly funded by drawing cash down (2,384M to 1,513M) and not refinancing 700M repaid in 2025; total liabilities 11.4B, debt 6.9B. Restructuring is ongoing (86M in 9M26, about 0.45 per share guided for the year). Ratings revenue depends on issuance cycles. Peers (SPGI, MSCI, FDS, VRSK), history, MD&A and litigation not read.
invalidation: MIS transaction revenue declines for two further quarters with investment-grade issuance also falling; MA ARR growth below 6%; adjusted operating margin below 50%; net debt/EBITDA above 2.5x because of buybacks; regulatory or litigation penalties in ratings; guided FCF cut below 2.5B.
